S82.01.note: The plan is read by the mobile billing screen; the cited apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts is not checked here.
steps: Open the side menu and tap Settings.
Tap Account, then the Subscription row (switch to AGI Cloud mode first if the Cloud rows are hidden).
Read the "Current plan" row on the Subscription screen.
Compare the plan name with the account's plan. It shows "Not confirmed" or "Checking…" while the server check is pending.
S82.01.where: Side menu > Settings > Account > Subscription (row shows the plan name); on the Subscription screen, the "Current plan" row

S82.02.needs: a paid account (the row is hidden on Free)
S82.02.note: Row only appears for a paid, entitled, non-Free plan; the Usage screen also shows "This billing period" with "Resets …" text.
steps: Open the side menu, tap Settings, then Account, then Subscription.
Find the row labelled Renews (or Access ends, or Trial ends) under Current plan.
Compare the date on that row with the renewal or end date expected for the account.
S82.02.where: Side menu > Settings > Account > Subscription > "Renews" row (or "Access ends" / "Trial ends")

S82.03.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees only the "Free plan" screen with an Upgrade button)
S82.03.note: Screen title "Usage" comes from the Settings Cloud group row in apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings.
Tap the Usage row in the Cloud group.
Under Plan usage, look at the bar labelled "This billing period" (the overall meter) and the "Current session" bar.
Compare each bar's fill and percent with the plan allowance.
S82.03.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Plan usage" section: bars "Current session", "Weekly limits" and "This billing period"

S82.04.needs: a paid account with usage in the period
S82.04.note: The card only lists rows once there are requests; the "flagship-model cap" bar is "Most capable models" under Weekly limits (packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts).
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to the "Where your usage went" card.
Read the "By model" list: each row shows a model name and its request and credit totals.
Compare the rows with the models used in the account.
S82.04.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By model" list

steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went".
Read the "By product area" list under the period rows.
Compare the rows with the Chat, AGI Work, Deep Research, AGI Code and Browser areas.
S82.05.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By product area" list

S82.06.needs: a paid account with a voice allowance
S82.06.note: The card is hidden when the account has no allowance data; the Voice row is built from the server's unit list, not checked against a live response.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Voice" row: it shows minutes used of the monthly amount, or "no monthly cap".
Compare with the voice minutes used in the period.
S82.06.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Voice" row

S82.07.needs: a paid account that has generated images this period
S82.07.note: The Images row only appears when the account has image requests in the period.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Images" row: image count and credits for the period.
Compare with the images generated this period.
S82.07.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Images" row

S82.08.needs: a paid account with a video allowance
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Video" row: seconds used of the monthly amount.
Compare with the video seconds generated in the period.
S82.08.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Video" row

S82.09.needs: a paid account that has run Deep Research
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went" and read "By product area".
Find the row labelled Deep Research and read its request and credit totals.
S82.09.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By product area" > "Deep Research" row

S82.10.needs: a paid account that has used AGI Work or AGI Code
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went" and read "By product area".
Find the rows labelled AGI Work (agentic work) and AGI Code (coding).
Compare their totals with the coding and agent runs made.
S82.10.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > "By product area" > "AGI Work" and "AGI Code" rows

S82.11.needs: a paid account with a storage limit
S82.11.note: The card is hidden when storage data is missing.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to the "File storage" card.
Read the "Used" row: used bytes of the plan limit, with a bar below it.
Compare with the files uploaded or generated.

S82.12.needs: a paid account, and a response that is still running
S82.12.note: The row only appears when the response allowance is returned by the server.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "This month" card.
Read the "Responses running now" row: active responses of the concurrent limit, "at a time".
Start a long response and compare the count.
S82.12.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "This month" card > "Responses running now" row

S82.13.note: Bonus and purchased rows only appear in builds where native purchases are on (NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE in apps/mobile/src/features/billing/nativePurchaseAvailability.ts).
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read "Included in your plan": credits left and the monthly total.
Compare with the credits expected to remain.
S82.13.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card ("Included in your plan" row, with "left" amount)

S82.14.needs: a paid account in a build with native purchases; a purchased-credit account to see amounts
S82.14.note: Without native purchases only "Included in your plan" shows.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read "Included in your plan" and "Purchased credits" side by side.
Compare that the two rows are separate balances.
S82.14.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card > "Included in your plan" and "Purchased credits" rows

S82.15.needs: an account that has bonus credits (referral or promotion); native-purchase build
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card.
Read the "Bonus credits" row: remaining amount and its "Next expiry" line, or "None".
Compare with a promotion or referral credit the account received.
S82.15.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card > "Bonus credits" row

S82.16.needs: an account with bonus or purchased credits
S82.16.note: Purchased-credit expiry text is built in the same file (purchasedRow) and is shown only where native purchases are on.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Find the "Credit balances" card and read the detail under "Bonus credits" ("Next expiry …") and "Purchased credits".
Read the "Resets" note on the "This month" card and the "Resets" card if present.
Compare the dates with each credit's lapse date.
S82.16.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Credit balances" card ("Next expiry" and purchase expiry lines) and "This month" card ("Resets …" note)

S82.17.needs: a paid account with active windows
S82.17.note: The visible text is built from hours, minutes and days; the exact wording is the template in the vocabulary file.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Under Plan usage, read the small line under each bar that starts "Resets in".
Wait a few minutes or compare with the clock and check the countdown moves.
S82.17.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Plan usage" section: a "Resets in …" line under each bar ("Current session", "Weekly limits", "This billing period")

S82.18.needs: a paid account with usage history
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud mode, then open Settings and tap Usage in the Cloud group.
Scroll to "Where your usage went".
Tap Days, then Weeks, then Months.
Compare that the period rows change to daily, weekly and monthly totals.
S82.18.where: Settings > Cloud > Usage > "Where your usage went" > segmented buttons "Days", "Weeks", "Months"

S82.20.needs: a cloud account with at least one agent run that reported usage
S82.20.note: The side-menu opener and the task list title were not confirmed; the Cost and Usage rows show only when run usage exists.
steps: Open the side menu and tap AGI Work.
Tap a task run in the list to open its details sheet.
Read the "Cost" row and the "Usage" row (calls and tokens) in the metadata area.
Compare with the task's work done.
S82.20.where: Side menu > AGI Work > open a finished task > details sheet with "Cost" and "Usage" rows

S82.23.needs: a cloud account with a finished agent run
S82.23.note: The Cost row is shown when run usage exists and reads "Metered against your free trial allowance" when there is no cost figure; the code does not check that the run has finished.
steps: Open the side menu, tap AGI Work, then tap a task run that has finished.
Read the "Cost" row in the details sheet.
Compare with the credits shown on the Usage screen for that period.
S82.23.where: Side menu > AGI Work > open a task run > "Cost" row in the details sheet

labels.text: You're close to the Free limit for now

S82.24.needs: a cloud account near a usage limit
S82.24.note: Banner shows at 25% remaining (warning) and 10% (critical) per packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts; reaching this state needs a near-limit account.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud on an account near a usage limit, then open any chat.
Look above the message box for the usage banner with a gauge icon.
Read the headline and the reset line under it.
Compare with the usage on the Usage screen: the banner appears when a window has 25% or less left.
S82.24.where: Chat screen > warning banner above the message box (e.g. "You're close to the Free limit for now" or "You have used … of …")

labels.text: You've reached the Free limit for now

S82.25.needs: an account at a usage limit (or a Free account after its allowance is used)
S82.25.note: Which title appears depends on the recovery action and whether native purchases are on; the sheet is opened from apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx.
steps: On an account at its limit, open a chat and send a message.
A bottom sheet opens: read its title and the body explaining which feature is blocked.
Read the reset line ("Resets in …") under the body, if shown.
Compare with the limit that was reached.
S82.25.where: Chat screen > send a message at the limit > bottom sheet titled "Choose a plan", "Upgrade to …" or "Update billing", with the reset line

S82.26.needs: an account at a limit where the server suggests a standard model
S82.26.note: The button appears only when the paywall presentation sets suggestStandardModel; how the eligible model is chosen was not traced.
steps: On an account at its limit, open a chat and send a message.
In the sheet that opens, look for the "Choose a standard model" button.
Tap it and check that the model picker offers another model the plan can use.
S82.26.where: Chat screen > send at the limit > bottom sheet > "Choose a standard model" button

labels.text: Add credits to keep going now, or wait for your usage to reset.

S82.27.needs: an account at or near a limit; a phone that allows notifications for the reminder
S82.27.note: There is no separate "wait" button; waiting is offered as copy and a reminder. The wait-only copy shows when the account cannot upgrade.
steps: On an account at its limit, open a chat and send a message, or look at the banner above the message box.
Read the recovery copy and the reset line: the banner or sheet shows when usage comes back.
Tap "Notify me when it resets" if it appears and check the confirmation "We’ll notify you".
S82.27.where: Chat screen > usage banner ("Notify me when it resets") and the send-time bottom sheet (reset line "Resets in …")
